$\mathbf{Extrema\ of\ the\ model\ } A/A_{\rm all}(\ell)\mathbf{:\ equations,\ sensitivities\ and\ merge\ points}$

This sheet writes the model behind Figs A10–A13 explicitly in its inputs, derives the condition that fixes the Galactic longitude $\ell$ of each maximum and minimum, gives the value of $A/A_{\rm all}$ there, the condition under which a maximum and a minimum merge, and the first- and second-order dependence of all four extrema on the four geometry inputs. Nothing here is fitted: every number is an exact root of the model equations, an implicit-function derivative, or a term of a series expansion.

## 1. Model and AF written in the inputs

Symbols. $\ell$: Galactic longitude [deg]; $\theta=\pi\ell/180$ [rad]. $D$: distance from the center of expansion (CoE) to the observer. $L$: scale length of the exponential core of the density profile. $x=D/L$. $d$: radius of the sampled shell of sources around the observer; $\varepsilon=d/D$. $\alpha$: dimensionless scale of the Gauss peculiar-velocity ansatz. $\kappa=GM(<D)/(D^3H^2)$: dimensionless mass inside the observer's radius. $H$: background (homologous) expansion rate; $G$: Newton's constant. $\mathrm{Amp}_A=-0.06$ and $\phi_A=0.35$ rad: amplitude and phase of the sine modulation. $f_u=0.94$: fixed share of the local density $\rho(D)$ carried by the uniform floor. $W$: width of the $\Delta\ell\approx90^\circ$ boxcar smoothing. Units: $G=H=D=1$, so lengths are in $D$, speeds in $HD$, masses in $D^3H^2/G$.

$$ A(\ell)=\left[1-\mathrm{Amp}_A\,\sin\left(\theta+\phi_A\right)\right]\,AF(\theta),\qquad\theta=\dfrac{\pi\,\ell}{180} \tag{1.1} $$

Geometry. The CoE sits at the origin and the observer at $\vec D=(1,0,0)$. A line of sight has unit vector $\hat n=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta,0)$, so $\theta=0$ points directly away from the CoE and $\theta=\pi$ toward it (the code identifies this angle with $\ell$ directly; the axis offset is carried by $\phi_A$). The source on the shell in that direction is at

$$ \vec r=\vec D+\varepsilon\,\hat n=\left(1+\varepsilon\cos\theta,\ \varepsilon\sin\theta,\ 0\right),\qquad r(\theta)=\sqrt{1+2\,\varepsilon\cos\theta+\varepsilon^2} \tag{1.2} $$

Mass. The density is an exponential core plus a uniform floor, $\rho(r)=\rho_{c0}\,\mathrm{e}^{-xr}+\rho_u$. The code first sets $\rho(1)=\Omega_m\rho_{\rm crit}$ with the floor holding the share $f_u$, then rescales every mass so that $m(1)=\kappa$. Integrating $4\pi r^2\rho$ and dividing by its value at $r=1$, the matter density $\Omega_m$, $\rho_{\rm crit}$, $G$ and $H$ all cancel, leaving

$$ N(x)=6\,(1-f_u)\left(\mathrm{e}^{x}-1-x-\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right)+f_u\,x^3 \tag{1.3} $$

$$ m(r)=\dfrac{\kappa}{N(x)}\left\{6\,(1-f_u)\left[\mathrm{e}^{x}-\mathrm{e}^{x(1-r)}\left(1+x\,r+\dfrac{x^2r^2}{2}\right)\right]+f_u\,x^3r^3\right\} \tag{1.4} $$

Velocity. Gauss peculiar-velocity ansatz (inward pull of the enclosed mass), in the units above:

$$ \vec u(\vec r)=-\alpha\,\dfrac{G\,m(r)}{r^3H}\,\vec r=-\alpha\,\dfrac{m(r)}{r^3}\,\vec r \tag{1.5} $$

Observed expansion rate along $\hat n$ (the differential radial velocity across the shell, divided by its radius). With $\vec u(\vec r)\cdot\hat n=-\alpha\,m(r)(\cos\theta+\varepsilon)/r^3$ and $\vec u(\vec D)\cdot\hat n=-\alpha\kappa\cos\theta$:

$$ \begin{aligned} &h(\theta)\equiv\dfrac{H_{\rm obs}(\theta)}{H}=1+\dfrac{\left[\vec u(\vec r)-\vec u(\vec D)\right]\cdot\hat n}{\varepsilon} \\ &=1+\dfrac{\alpha}{\varepsilon}\left[\kappa\cos\theta-\dfrac{m(r)\,(\cos\theta+\varepsilon)}{r^3}\right] \end{aligned} \tag{1.6} $$

Substituting (1.4), fully in the inputs:

$$ \begin{aligned} &h(\theta)=1+\dfrac{\alpha\kappa}{\varepsilon}\cos\theta-\dfrac{\alpha\kappa\,(\cos\theta+\varepsilon)}{\varepsilon\,r^3\,N(x)} \\ &\times\left\{6\,(1-f_u)\left[\mathrm{e}^{x}-\mathrm{e}^{x(1-r)}\left(1+x\,r+\dfrac{x^2r^2}{2}\right)\right]+f_u\,x^3r^3\right\} \end{aligned} \tag{1.7} $$

Two consequences. (i) $\alpha$ and $\kappa$ enter only through the product $\alpha\kappa$, so the $\alpha$ and $\kappa$ sweeps trace the same family of curves. (ii) The code's AF mode "hratio" uses $A_{\rm raw}=H_{\rm obs}/H=h$; its floor $H_{\rm obs}\geq10^{-6}H$ never acts on the swept ranges (smallest $h$ there is 0.30).

Smoothing and normalisation. The code divides $h$ by its sky mean and applies a wrap-around boxcar of 91 samples on its 361-point grid, i.e. width $W=91\times360^\circ/361=90.75^\circ$. As an integral:

$$ AF(\theta)=\dfrac{1}{W\,\bar h}\int_{\theta-W/2}^{\theta+W/2}h(\theta^\prime)\,d\theta^\prime,\qquad\bar h=\dfrac{1}{2\pi}\int_{0}^{2\pi}h(\theta)\,d\theta,\qquad W=\dfrac{182\,\pi}{361} \tag{1.8} $$

The core term contains $\mathrm{e}^{-x\,r(\theta)}$ with $r(\theta)=\sqrt{1+2\varepsilon\cos\theta+\varepsilon^2}$, which has no elementary antiderivative in $\theta$ (only the floor term integrates in closed form). So $AF$ itself stays a one-dimensional integral. Its slope and curvature do not: by the fundamental theorem of calculus they are differences of $h$ and $h^\prime$ at the two window edges.

$$ \dfrac{\partial AF}{\partial\theta}=\dfrac{h\left(\theta+\frac{W}{2}\right)-h\left(\theta-\frac{W}{2}\right)}{W\,\bar h},\qquad\dfrac{\partial^2 AF}{\partial\theta^2}=\dfrac{h^\prime\left(\theta+\frac{W}{2}\right)-h^\prime\left(\theta-\frac{W}{2}\right)}{W\,\bar h} \tag{1.9} $$

Differentiating (1.7), using $dr/d\theta=-\varepsilon\sin\theta/r$ and $dm/dr=3\kappa x^3r^2\left[(1-f_u)\mathrm{e}^{x(1-r)}+f_u\right]/N(x)$; in $r\,dm/dr-3m$ the floor cancels exactly, leaving:

$$ \begin{aligned} &h^\prime(\theta)=\dfrac{\alpha\kappa\sin\theta}{\varepsilon}\left\{\dfrac{6\,(1-f_u)\left[\mathrm{e}^{x}-\mathrm{e}^{x(1-r)}\left(1+x\,r+\frac{x^2r^2}{2}\right)\right]+f_u\,x^3r^3}{r^3\,N(x)}-1\right. \\ &\left.-\dfrac{18\,(1-f_u)\,\varepsilon\,(\cos\theta+\varepsilon)}{r^5\,N(x)}\left[\mathrm{e}^{x}-\mathrm{e}^{x(1-r)}\left(1+x\,r+\dfrac{x^2r^2}{2}+\dfrac{x^3r^3}{6}\right)\right]\right\} \end{aligned} \tag{1.10} $$

Check: (1.1)–(1.8) reproduce the code's plotted curve at baseline to 4.7e-06 (max abs difference over 361 points), and (1.10) matches a numerical derivative of (1.7) to 2e-10.

## 2. Extremum condition

Setting $dA/d\ell=0$ (Chris's form), with $\partial AF/\partial\ell=(\pi/180)\,\partial AF/\partial\theta$ from (1.9):

$$ -\mathrm{Amp}_A\,\dfrac{\pi}{180}\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi\ell}{180}+\phi_A\right)AF+\left[1-\mathrm{Amp}_A\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi\ell}{180}+\phi_A\right)\right]\dfrac{\partial AF}{\partial\ell}=0 \tag{2.1} $$

Multiplying by $180\,W\bar h/\pi$ and inserting (1.8)–(1.9), the normalisation $\bar h$ cancels. The extremum angles $\theta_k=\pi\ell_k/180$ ($k=1..4$) are the roots of

$$ \begin{aligned} &\left[1-\mathrm{Amp}_A\sin\left(\theta_k+\phi_A\right)\right]\left[h\left(\theta_k+\dfrac{W}{2}\right)-h\left(\theta_k-\dfrac{W}{2}\right)\right] \\ &=\ \mathrm{Amp}_A\cos\left(\theta_k+\phi_A\right)\int_{\theta_k-W/2}^{\theta_k+W/2}h(\theta^\prime)\,d\theta^\prime \end{aligned} \tag{2.2} $$

with $h$ from (1.7). Plain words: the slope of the smoothed curve is set by how different $h$ is at the two edges of the 90° window, and the sine factor tilts it in proportion to the area under $h$ inside the window. Because $h$ contains $\mathrm{e}^{-x\sqrt{1+2\varepsilon\cos\theta+\varepsilon^2}}$ and the integral has no elementary form, (2.2) is transcendental in $\theta_k$: there is no exact closed form for $\ell_k$. It is solved numerically (bracketed root on a 0.25° scan, then Brent to $10^{-13}$ rad). A closed form exists only as a series in small $\varepsilon$ and small $\mathrm{Amp}_A$ (Section 6).

Type of extremum, from the second derivative ($<0$ maximum, $>0$ minimum):

$$ \begin{aligned} &\dfrac{\partial^2A}{\partial\theta^2}=\mathrm{Amp}_A\sin\left(\theta+\phi_A\right)AF-2\,\mathrm{Amp}_A\cos\left(\theta+\phi_A\right)\dfrac{\partial AF}{\partial\theta} \\ &+\left[1-\mathrm{Amp}_A\sin\left(\theta+\phi_A\right)\right]\dfrac{\partial^2AF}{\partial\theta^2} \end{aligned} \tag{2.3} $$

## 3. Extremum value

$$ A^*_k=A(\ell_k)=\left[1-\mathrm{Amp}_A\sin\left(\theta_k+\phi_A\right)\right]\dfrac{1}{W\bar h}\int_{\theta_k-W/2}^{\theta_k+W/2}h(\theta^\prime)\,d\theta^\prime \tag{3.1} $$

Using (2.2) to replace the integral (valid wherever $\cos(\theta_k+\phi_A)\neq0$), the value needs only $h$ at the two window edges and $\bar h$:

$$ A^*_k=\dfrac{\left[1-\mathrm{Amp}_A\sin\left(\theta_k+\phi_A\right)\right]^2\left[h\left(\theta_k+\frac{W}{2}\right)-h\left(\theta_k-\frac{W}{2}\right)\right]}{\mathrm{Amp}_A\cos\left(\theta_k+\phi_A\right)\,W\,\bar h} \tag{3.2} $$

Check: (3.2) equals (3.1) at all four baseline extrema to 3e-13. Baseline $\bar h=0.89016$ ($\alpha=1$) and 0.85720 ($\alpha=1.3$). Because $\partial A/\partial\theta=0$ at $\theta_k$, the shift of the angle does not change the value at first order (envelope theorem):

$$ \dfrac{dA^*_k}{dp}=\left.\dfrac{\partial A}{\partial p}\right|_{\theta=\theta_k},\qquad p\in\{x,\ \varepsilon,\ \alpha,\ \kappa\} \tag{3.3} $$

## 4. Merge (fold) condition

A maximum and a minimum merge and vanish where the curve has a horizontal inflection: (2.2) and (2.3) vanish together. With one input $p$ free and the others at baseline, this is two equations in two unknowns $(\theta_f,\,p_f)$:

$$ \left.\dfrac{\partial A}{\partial\theta}\right|_{\theta_f,\,p_f}=0\quad\mathrm{[eq.\ 2.2]},\qquad\left.\dfrac{\partial^2A}{\partial\theta^2}\right|_{\theta_f,\,p_f}=0\quad\mathrm{[eq.\ 2.3]} \tag{4.1} $$

| free input | fold from (4.1) | $\ell_f$ [deg] | $A_f$ | sweep (bisection) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D/L | 3.15684 | 127.46 | 1.02306 | 3.15674 |
| α | 0.30560 | 127.03 | 1.02514 | 0.30558 |
| κ | 0.07047 | 127.03 | 1.02514 | outside 0.15–0.70 |
| d/D (α=1.3) | 0.96413 | 134.94 | 0.92910 | outside 0.06–0.74 |

The two systems close to residuals of order $10^{-16}$ and agree with the sweep values to $10^{-4}$ (the sweep used the code's 1° sampled curve). The merging pair is always the maximum near 170° and the minimum near 95°. Since only $\alpha\kappa$ enters, the $\alpha$ fold sits at $\alpha\kappa=0.0705$, so at $\alpha=1$ a $\kappa$ fold would need $\kappa=0.0705$, below the swept $0.15$–$0.70$; that is why the $\kappa$ sweep shows no merge (solving (4.1) directly in $\kappa$ gives the same 0.0705). In $d/D$ ($\alpha=1.3$) no pair meets inside the swept 0.06–0.74; the maximum near 173° and the minimum near 94° drift together and merge at $d/D=0.9641$ ($\ell_f=134.9^\circ$). Just beyond, at $d/D=0.9673$, a new max–min pair is born near $\ell=204^\circ$, because the sampled shell then nearly touches the CoE ($r\to1-\varepsilon$ at $\theta=\pi$) and the model becomes singular at $d/D=1$.

Near a fold the two merging extrema move as a square root, not linearly. Keeping the leading terms of $\partial A/\partial\theta$ around $(\theta_f,p_f)$, where $A_{\theta\theta}=0$: $A_{\theta p}\,\delta p+\frac{1}{2}A_{\theta\theta\theta}\,\delta\theta^2=0$, so

$$ \ell_\pm\approx\ell_f\pm\dfrac{180}{\pi}\sqrt{-\dfrac{2\,A_{\theta p}}{A_{\theta\theta\theta}}\,\left(p-p_f\right)} \tag{4.2} $$

with $A_{\theta p}=\partial^2A/\partial\theta\partial p$ and $A_{\theta\theta\theta}=\partial^3A/\partial\theta^3$ at the fold. Numerically $\ell_\pm\approx127.5^\circ\pm33.3^\circ\sqrt{D/L-3.1568}$ and $\ell_\pm\approx127.0^\circ\pm82.2^\circ\sqrt{\alpha-0.3056}$ (upper sign: the maximum). This square-root behaviour is why straight Taylor series in $D/L$ and $\alpha$ (Section 5) fail toward the low ends of those sweeps.

## 5. Sensitivities around baseline (implicit-function derivatives)

Baseline: $x=5.9$, $\varepsilon=0.1$, $\alpha=1$, $\kappa=0.230588$ (Figs A10–A12). The A13 hold ($\alpha=1.3$) is a second base point, used for the $d/D$ sweep. Diagonal Taylor forms (one input varied at a time):

$$ \begin{aligned} &\ell_k\approx\ell_{k,0}+\sum_p\dfrac{\partial\ell_k}{\partial p}\left(p-p_0\right)+\dfrac{1}{2}\sum_p\dfrac{\partial^2\ell_k}{\partial p^2}\left(p-p_0\right)^2 \\ &A^*_k\approx A^*_{k,0}+\sum_p\dfrac{\partial A^*_k}{\partial p}\left(p-p_0\right)+\dfrac{1}{2}\sum_p\dfrac{\partial^2A^*_k}{\partial p^2}\left(p-p_0\right)^2 \end{aligned} \tag{5.1} $$

Cross terms $\partial^2/\partial p\,\partial q$ are not included. With $F=\partial A/\partial\theta$ from (2.1)–(2.2) and subscripts denoting partial derivatives at $(\theta_k,p_0)$:

$$ \begin{aligned} &\dfrac{\partial\theta_k}{\partial p}=-\dfrac{F_p}{F_\theta},\qquad\dfrac{\partial^2\theta_k}{\partial p^2}=-\dfrac{F_{pp}+2F_{\theta p}\,\theta_k^\prime+F_{\theta\theta}\,\theta_k^{\prime\,2}}{F_\theta} \\ &\dfrac{\partial A^*_k}{\partial p}=A_p,\qquad\dfrac{\partial^2A^*_k}{\partial p^2}=A_{pp}+F_p\,\theta_k^\prime,\qquad\theta_k^\prime\equiv\dfrac{\partial\theta_k}{\partial p} \end{aligned} \tag{5.2} $$

$F_\theta=\partial^2A/\partial\theta^2$ is evaluated from (2.3) analytically; the $p$-partials by central differences of the exact model. Each first and second derivative was cross-checked against central differences of the exact roots (agreement to 4–5 significant figures). Because only $\alpha\kappa$ enters, $\partial/\partial\alpha=\kappa\,\partial/\partial\kappa$ at $\alpha=1$, visible in the tables.

## 6. Closed form to first order in $\varepsilon$ and $\mathrm{Amp}_A$

Expanding (1.6) in $\varepsilon$ to first order (Taylor series of $\vec u$ along $\hat n$ about $\vec D$) turns $h$ into four harmonics. With $\mu_1\equiv m^\prime(1)/\kappa=3x^3/N(x)$ and $\mu_2\equiv m^{\prime\prime}(1)/\kappa=3x^3\left[2-x(1-f_u)\right]/N(x)$, expanded:

$$ h(\theta)\approx h_0+h_1\cos\theta+h_2\cos2\theta+h_3\cos3\theta+O(\varepsilon^2) \tag{6.1} $$

$$ h_0=1-\dfrac{\alpha\kappa}{2}\left[\dfrac{3x^3}{N(x)}-1\right],\qquad h_2=-\dfrac{\alpha\kappa}{2}\left[\dfrac{3x^3}{N(x)}-3\right] \tag{6.2} $$

$$ \begin{aligned} &h_1=-\dfrac{9\,\alpha\varepsilon\kappa}{8}\left[1-\dfrac{x^3\left(1+x(1-f_u)\right)}{N(x)}\right] \\ &h_3=-\dfrac{3\,\alpha\varepsilon\kappa}{8}\left[5-\dfrac{x^3\left(5+x(1-f_u)\right)}{N(x)}\right] \end{aligned} \tag{6.3} $$

The boxcar multiplies harmonic $j$ by $\sin(jW/2)/(jW/2)$, and the mean is $h_0$ to this order, so

$$ AF(\theta)\approx1+a_1\cos\theta+a_2\cos2\theta+a_3\cos3\theta,\qquad a_j=\dfrac{h_j}{h_0}\,\dfrac{\sin\left(jW/2\right)}{jW/2} \tag{6.4} $$

Baseline ($\alpha=1$): $h_0=0.89029$, $a_1=-0.00312$, $a_2=0.08572$, $a_3=-0.00430$; the quadrupole $a_2$ dominates. With $\mathrm{Amp}_A=0$ the extrema of (6.4) are at $\theta=0$, $\theta=\pi$ and at $\pm\theta_c$ with

$$ \cos\theta_c=\dfrac{-a_2+\sqrt{a_2^2-3\,a_3\left(a_1-3a_3\right)}}{6\,a_3}\qquad\left(\mathrm{the\ root\ with\ }\left|\cos\theta_c\right|\leq1\right) \tag{6.5} $$

The sine factor then shifts each $\theta_{k,0}\in\{0,\ \theta_c,\ \pi,\ 2\pi-\theta_c\}$ to first order in $\mathrm{Amp}_A$:

$$ \begin{aligned} &\ell_k\approx\dfrac{180}{\pi}\left[\theta_{k,0}+\dfrac{\mathrm{Amp}_A\cos\left(\theta_{k,0}+\phi_A\right)\,AF(\theta_{k,0})}{AF^{\prime\prime}(\theta_{k,0})}\right] \\ &A^*_k\approx\left[1-\mathrm{Amp}_A\sin\left(\theta_{k,0}+\phi_A\right)\right]AF(\theta_{k,0}) \\ &AF^{\prime\prime}(\theta)=-a_1\cos\theta-4a_2\cos2\theta-9a_3\cos3\theta \end{aligned} \tag{6.6} $$

Simplest explicit form ($\varepsilon\to0$, so $a_1=a_3=0$ and $\theta_c=\pi/2$). The four extrema are then fully explicit in the inputs, with $a_2=\dfrac{\sin W}{W}\,\dfrac{\alpha\kappa\left[3-3x^3/N(x)\right]}{2-\alpha\kappa\left[3x^3/N(x)-1\right]}$:

$$ \begin{aligned} &\ell_1\approx-\dfrac{180}{\pi}\,\dfrac{\mathrm{Amp}_A\cos\phi_A\,(1+a_2)}{4a_2} \\ &\ell_2\approx90^\circ-\dfrac{180}{\pi}\,\dfrac{\mathrm{Amp}_A\sin\phi_A\,(1-a_2)}{4a_2} \\ &\ell_3\approx180^\circ+\dfrac{180}{\pi}\,\dfrac{\mathrm{Amp}_A\cos\phi_A\,(1+a_2)}{4a_2} \\ &\ell_4\approx270^\circ+\dfrac{180}{\pi}\,\dfrac{\mathrm{Amp}_A\sin\phi_A\,(1-a_2)}{4a_2} \end{aligned} \tag{6.7} $$

$$ \begin{aligned} &A^*_1\approx(1-\mathrm{Amp}_A\sin\phi_A)(1+a_2),\quad A^*_2\approx(1-\mathrm{Amp}_A\cos\phi_A)(1-a_2) \\ &A^*_3\approx(1+\mathrm{Amp}_A\sin\phi_A)(1+a_2),\quad A^*_4\approx(1+\mathrm{Amp}_A\cos\phi_A)(1-a_2) \end{aligned} \tag{6.8} $$

Baseline ($\alpha=1$), exact vs closed forms ($\ell_k$ / $A^*_k$):

| extremum k | exact (2.2), (3.1) | O(ε), (6.5)–(6.6) | ε→0, (6.7)–(6.8) |
|---|---|---|---|
| k=1 max | 10.43° / 1.1061 | 11.57° / 1.1005 | 10.23° / 1.1081 |
| k=2 min | 95.34° / 0.9645 | 94.99° / 0.9651 | 93.14° / 0.9658 |
| k=3 max | 170.09° / 1.0758 | 170.82° / 1.0706 | 169.77° / 1.0634 |
| k=4 min | 265.73° / 0.8617 | 265.50° / 0.8621 | 266.86° / 0.8627 |

Validity: the expansion assumes $\varepsilon\ll1$ (the $O(\varepsilon^2)$ harmonics are dropped) and $|\mathrm{Amp}_A\,AF/AF^{\prime\prime}|\ll1$ (the sine tilt is small next to the quadrupole curvature, i.e. $|\mathrm{Amp}_A|\ll4a_2$). It is within 2° of the exact extrema for D/L ≥ 4.9, α ≥ 0.73, the whole κ range 0.17–0.70, and d/D ≤ 0.32 (table above). It breaks down as $a_2$ shrinks toward $|\mathrm{Amp}_A|/4=0.015$: at both folds $a_2\approx0.025$ (it is 0.086 at baseline), and it also fails for large $d/D$.
